title: EVERY EARTHQUAKE WAS A REMINDER THAT OUR ONLY SECURITY IS THROUGH JESUS CHRIST
paragraphs: EVERY EARTHQUAKE WAS A REMINDER THAT OUR ONLY SECURITY IS THROUGH JESUS CHRIST
The dishes rattled first.
A faint trembling beneath the floor.
Then the walls groaned.
The ground moved.
And for a few terrifying moments, humanity was reminded of something it desperately tries to forget:
We are not as secure as we think we are.
In a world obsessed with stability, earthquakes expose a truth we spend most of our lives trying to bury.
Nothing beneath our feet is truly permanent.
Not our homes.
Not our savings.
Not our governments.
Not our plans.
Not even the earth itself.
The moment the ground shakes, every illusion of control begins to crumble.
And perhaps that is why earthquakes have always carried a spiritual weight throughout Scripture.
Not because God delights in fear.
But because He loves truth.
And few things reveal truth faster than realizing the very ground beneath you can move.
The Hebrew Scriptures repeatedly use the language of trembling earth as a reminder that creation itself responds to the presence, holiness, power, and judgment of God.
The Psalmist wrote:
"The earth shook and trembled; the foundations also of the hills moved and were shaken, because He was angry." (Psalm 18:7)
The Hebrew word used for "shook" is רָעַשׁ (ra'ash), carrying the imagery of violent trembling, quaking, and upheaval.
It is not merely geological language.
It is theological language.
Creation itself testifies that humanity is not in control.
Modern society has mastered comfort.
But comfort often produces a dangerous illusion.
We begin believing our security comes from our careers.
Our investments.
Our insurance policies.
Our political systems.
Our technology.
Our influence.
Our reputation.
Yet history repeatedly proves how fragile those things truly are.
One earthquake.
One diagnosis.
One accident.
One phone call.
One unexpected loss.
And everything we built our identity upon can collapse overnight.
Jesus addressed this very issue long before modern skyscrapers existed.
In Matthew 7:24-27, He told a story that remains one of the most powerful illustrations ever spoken.
A wise man built his house upon the rock.
A foolish man built his house upon the sand.
The storms came.
The winds blew.
The floods rose.
Both houses faced the same trial.
The difference was not the storm.
The difference was the foundation.
The Greek word Christ used for rock is πέτρα (petra), meaning bedrock, massive stone, an immovable foundation.
The foolish builder trusted what appeared stable.
The wise builder trusted what actually was stable.
This distinction changes everything.
Many people mistake visible strength for actual security.
A beautiful house can hide a weak foundation.
A successful life can hide a broken soul.
A smiling face can conceal unbearable anxiety.
A full bank account can coexist with spiritual bankruptcy.
Jesus was never interested in making people look secure.
He came to make them secure.
And true security can only be found in Him.
The reality is uncomfortable.
Earthquakes do not create insecurity.
They reveal it.
The shaking simply exposes what was already unstable.
The same is true spiritually.
Many of us discover where our trust truly rests only when life begins to shake.
When health disappears.
When relationships fracture.
When jobs vanish.
When dreams die.
When prayers seem unanswered.
When the future becomes uncertain.
Suddenly we discover whether our faith was resting in God or merely resting in circumstances.
The prophet Isaiah delivered a message that speaks directly into this tension.
"You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on You, because he trusts in You." (Isaiah 26:3)
The phrase "perfect peace" comes from the Hebrew שָׁלוֹם שָׁלוֹם (shalom shalom).
The repetition is intentional.
It communicates complete peace.
Whole peace.
Undivided peace.
A peace that circumstances cannot manufacture and disasters cannot remove.
This peace is not found in stable ground.
It is found in a stable Savior.
That truth became unmistakably clear on a hill called Golgotha.
The greatest shaking in human history was not geological.
It was spiritual.
Humanity stood guilty before a holy God.
Sin had fractured everything.
Every heart.
Every family.
Every nation.
Every generation.
We were separated from God and incapable of repairing the damage ourselves.
Then Jesus stepped into our scandal.
The perfect Son of God entered a broken world.
The One who created the mountains allowed Himself to be nailed to wood.
The One who spoke galaxies into existence was mocked by the people He came to save.
The One who deserved eternal worship accepted temporary humiliation.
And in doing so, He rewrote everything.
Matthew records a remarkable detail surrounding Christ's death:
"And behold, the curtain of the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom. And the earth shook, and the rocks were split." (Matthew 27:51)
The Greek text says:

ἐσείσθη ἡ γῆ
(eseisthē hē gē)
"The earth was shaken."
Even creation responded.
The cross was not merely another execution.
It was the turning point of history.
Sin was being defeated.
Justice was being satisfied.
Mercy was being extended.
Grace was being unleashed.
The scandal of humanity was meeting the grace of God.
And because of Jesus, the shaking no longer has the final word.
That is the hope many people desperately need today.
The Christian life is not a promise that earthquakes will never come.
It is the promise that Christ remains unshaken when they do.
Hebrews 12:28 declares:
"Therefore let us be grateful for receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken."
The phrase "cannot be shaken" comes from the Greek word ἀσάλευτος (asaleutos).
Immovable.
Permanent.
Unshakable.
The kingdoms of this world rise and fall.
Markets fluctuate.
Governments change.
Empires collapse.
Civilizations disappear.
But the Kingdom of Christ remains.
Forever.
The greatest tragedy is not losing earthly security.
The greatest tragedy is trusting earthly security more than Jesus.
Many people spend their lives reinforcing walls while neglecting foundations.
They prepare for every disaster except eternity.
They insure everything except their souls.
They protect possessions while ignoring the condition of their hearts.
Yet every earthquake whispers the same message.
Every trembling floor.
Every shaking wall.
Every rattling window.
Every moment of uncertainty.
It reminds us that security was never meant to be found in creation.
It was always meant to be found in the Creator.
Perhaps that is why some of the strongest believers are not those who have experienced the least shaking.
Often they are the ones who have experienced the most.
They have watched dreams collapse.
They have buried loved ones.
They have endured heartbreak.
They have walked through betrayal.
They have faced impossible circumstances.
And somehow they emerge with a deeper confidence than before.
Not because life became easier.
But because Jesus became more real.
Their faith no longer rests upon outcomes.
It rests upon Christ.
That kind of faith cannot be manufactured.
It is forged in the shaking.
Maybe that describes your story.
Perhaps the ground beneath your life feels unstable right now.
Perhaps things you once trusted are crumbling.
Perhaps fear has become a constant companion.
Perhaps uncertainty has stolen your peace.
If so, hear the invitation of Christ.
Not an invitation to pretend everything is fine.
Not an invitation to deny reality.
But an invitation to build your life upon the only foundation that will never fail.
Jesus Christ.
The same Savior who calmed storms.
The same Savior who conquered death.
The same Savior who forgave sinners.
The same Savior who rose from the grave.
The same Savior who still rewrites lives today.
Because every earthquake ultimately points beyond itself.
Every tremor reminds us of a greater reality.
This world is not our final home.
Our hope is not found beneath our feet.
Our hope is found at the feet of Jesus.
And when everything else shakes, He remains.
Always.
Sit with it.
Pray through it.
The Gospel must continue reaching hearts that are searching for hope, healing, truth, and salvation.
One day the earth will shake for the last time—but those anchored to Christ will never have to fear the fall.
